_note: WO-672 Slice D + WO-892 + WO-1352 - structure damage-state thresholds for StructureDamageVisuals. HP-fraction thresholds: <= scuffOnset = the WO-1352 SCUFF band, a shader-parameter surface tell (albedo darkened by a SCALAR, plus smoothness dropped to matte) applied in scuffSteps discrete steps between scuffOnset and smolder; <= smolder = thin smoke wisp (Damage_Smolder); <= fire = flame + smoke volume (Damage_Fire); <= criticalBeacon = an ADDITIONAL fast-strobing alarm loop plus a '!' glyph (Damage_CriticalBeacon) meaning 'repair me NOW before it is destroyed'; broken (hp==0) = one-shot Damage_BreakBurst at the break transition + a persistent Damage_Ruin column, and the beacon STOPS (a destroyed structure cannot be saved - WO-753: destroyed is gone, it returns only via a full-cost rebuild). WO-892 moved these off Ember_Burn/Raid_Explosion: Ember_Burn pointed at a Hovl path that does not exist so it never reached the catalog and never rendered, and Raid_Explosion pointed into the gitignored Hovl pack. WO-1352 (owner ruling 2026-09-02) exists because RepairTarget.NeedsRepair is DamageFraction > 0.0001 while the first visible tell was the smolder at 0.5 - so 50%..99.99% HP was PRISTINE to the player and DAMAGED to the code, and Repair-All charged for it. scuffOnset MUST stay at or above 1 - that epsilon or the silent repair-eligible band re-opens; StructureBurnRegression's scuff oracle pins it. The five states read in GREYSCALE by surface value, smoke density, flame presence, pulse rhythm and layer count - never by tint (the owner is red/green colourblind); the scuff multiplies R, G and B by the IDENTICAL factor so hue and saturation are mathematically unchanged and only value moves. maxBurnLoops and maxCriticalBeacons are SEPARATE worst-first caps on top of VFXManager's global 20-loop cap; a structure holds at most one burn/ruin loop AND at most one beacon, so the worst case this system can hold is maxBurnLoops + maxCriticalBeacons. The scuff holds NO loop, NO particle and NO GameObject, so it needs no cap. WO-1352 FOLLOW-UP (2026-09-02, owner-delegated SME ruling): the first shipped values were measured on device as invisible - an Archer Tower at hp 0.960 took scuff step 1, which was a 12% albedo darkening and, because the ramp interpolates on (step-1)/(steps-1), a smoothness multiplier of EXACTLY 1.00. So the loudest thing about the first point of damage was a one-channel 12% value drop in daylight. The band is now FRONT-LOADED rather than linear: scuffSteps 3 -> 4, scuffMinDarken 0.12 -> 0.20, scuffMaxDarken 0.34 -> 0.38, and a NEW scuffGlossStep1 (0.55) gives the gloss ramp a step-1 endpoint of its own so the specular sheen dies at first blood instead of at the smolder. Ladder: step 1 albedo x0.80 gloss x0.55; step 2 x0.74 / x0.45; step 3 x0.68 / x0.35; step 4 x0.62 / x0.25. The pristine -> step 1 jump is 3.3x the albedo jump and 4.5x the gloss jump of any rung after it, because step 1 is the only rung with no rung above it to be compared against, and because 'this took a hit' is the one distinction a player actually reads off a building. The CEILING is deliberate too: most structures sit near full HP most of the time, so step 1 is what a healthy town looks like after a graze - it must read on INSPECTION, never at a glance, which is why the extra visibility was bought with the SECOND channel and not with a bigger colour hit. Escalation is untouched: scuff is still a static surface change, the smolder still adds motion and smoke, fire still adds a flame, critical still adds rhythm, broken still changes the silhouette. StructureBurnRegression's scuff oracle section E pins the step-1 floor AND ceiling, the two-channel requirement, the front-loading, strict monotonicity on both channels, and that the tint stays a pure scalar (hue/saturation unchanged, greyscale luma scaling by the same factor). perType keys are lowercase structure kinds; optOut skips the shared tells for types with bespoke damage presentation (gate force-field collapse, heart crystal states). Dual-copy rule: keep Assets/StreamingAssets/Data/Canonical/damage-states.json byte-identical.
